thread:
rachel_sales: Heads-up: HealthCore wants a short POC for Private deployment. Key constraints: no outbound internet from app subnets, central model bucket in our AWS account, prefer interface endpoints only (no TGW if possible) due to their org politics. They also want short-lived credentials for provisioning. Can we do a PrivateLink-first design?

theo_se: PrivateLink for control plane + customer VPC S3 endpoint for model pulls is the straightforward pattern. We can publish an EndpointService backed by an NLB in our account. Customer creates an Interface VPCE; SG on VPCE allows traffic from their app subnets. For model S3 access, use a Gateway endpoint in their account with a cross-account bucket policy that restricts access by VPC or VPCE id.

nina_infra: Quick Q: can our service assume an IAM role in the customer's account to write logs to their S3 or read configs? They don't want any long-lived keys on instances.

alvaro_netops: We usually recommend letting our agent fetch model manifests via PrivateLink control plane and then the model artifacts come from our model-account S3. Two options: 1) Customer creates a gateway endpoint to our S3 bucket via cross-account bucket policy and we whitelist their account/VPC; or 2) Customer routes outbound to a central egress VPC with tightly filtered NAT that can call our S3. Option 1 is better for 'no internet' requirement.

theo_se: Example S3 bucket policy snippet to restrict GetObject to their gateway VPCE: ```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedwoodModelFetcher"},
      "Action": "s3:GetObject",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-models-prod/*",
      "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:sourceVpce": "vpce-0abcde12345fgh678"}}
    }
  ]
}
```

alvaro_netops: Note: gateway endpoints don't support aws:sourceVpce, only interface endpoints do for condition contexts. For gateway endpoint you can restrict by aws:sourceVpc or aws:sourceVpcArn. Double-check.

theo_se: Good catch. Updated snippet for gateway endpoint (restrict by sourceVpc): ```json
{"Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:sourceVpc": "vpc-0a1b2c3d4e5f"}}}
```

nina_infra: For the control plane Interface Endpoint, what SG rules should we publish? We need exact ports to open in their app subnets.

theo_se: Control plane is HTTPS (443) to the NLB. SG on the customer's VPCE should allow outbound 443 to our NLB IPs, but we also require the NLB SG to allow inbound from the VPCE's security group. For health checks, use TCP 443 only. No other ports.

rachel_sales: They asked about credential rotation. Can we issue ephemeral creds for the POC so they don't have long-lived keys stuck in infra?

theo_se: Yes — we can issue session tokens via our bootstrap flow. For infra automation we support an assume-role-with-web-identity-like flow: customer infra calls our auth endpoint with a short-lived bootstrap token we issue during sales handoff. That token is exchangeable for ephemeral API creds scoped to the POC pool and expires after the POC window.

sec-bot: Security checklist added: network diagram, list of CIDRs, VPCE IDs, required KMS policy if they want encrypted model artifacts, and proof that no EC2 instance has public IPs in app subnets.

alvaro_netops: Action items: (1) Theo - draft NLB placement guidance (2AZs, subnets in registered account), show SG pairings for VPCE <-> NLB; (2) Rachel - capture HealthCore VPCE id + app VPC id + list of private subnets; (3) Nina - confirm whether they want gateway endpoint or prefer interface endpoint to S3 (interface endpoints give better per-VPCE restriction but higher cost).

rachel_sales: Scheduling kickoff with HealthCore infra for Tue 9am ET. I'll paste SOC checklist and ask for the VPCE and VPC details before the call.
